summary: Returns the value as an empty value, or throws.
description: Emptiness is read per kind: `null` and `undefined`, a string with nothing but whitespace, an array, `Set` or `Map` with no entries, an object with no own keys. `0` and `false` are values, not emptiness.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

params.message: The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted.
params.strict: When `true`, a string counts as empty only if it has no characters at all; by default whitespace is trimmed first.

returns: the same value, typed as an empty value.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
requireEmpty(null); // => null
requireEmpty(""); // => ""
requireEmpty(0); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireEmpty(false); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
